plan: With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the symmetric Bayesian-Nash equilibrium bid for a first-price auction is (n-1)/n times my value, i.e., (2/3)*15 = $10. Bidding my true value would give zero expected profit, so shading down balances win probability against profit margin. I'll bid $10 to maximize expected profit given the equilibrium strategy.

With 3 bidders and independent uniform values on [0,49], the symmetric Nash equilibrium bidding strategy is to bid (n-1)/n of your value, which balances winning probability against overpaying. Here n=3, so optimal bid ≈ (2/3)*36 = 24. This maximizes expected profit by shading appropriately below true value while remaining competitive against similarly rational opponents.

With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the optimal first-price auction strategy is to shade my bid to (n-1)/n of my value, i.e., bid = value × 2/3. This balances the trade-off between winning probability and profit margin. My value is $42, so I calculate 42 × 2/3 = 28. This bid maximizes expected profit against equally rational opponents using similar strategies.
